name: GGUF Q6_K (6-bit K-quant)
bits: 6.5633 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); block_q6_K is 6.5625 bpw (source comment) - Q6_K is essentially a pure type
quality_delta: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.35 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.03, within noise); unweighted mean 69.23 vs 69.47; size 6283 MiB (-58.98%). GSM8K reported 58.98 vs 77.63 for F16, which is a 18-point drop inconsistent with a +0.03 perplexity change and with the paper's own claim that Q6_K is near-baseline - treat the Q6_K GSM8K cell as unverified.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-10-04: was 256. Base type Q6_K has a 16-value scale group: dequantize_row_q6_K indexes `int is = l/16; y[l+0] = d*sc[is+0]*q1; ...` with `sc += 8` per 128 values - 16 int8 sub-block scales per 256-value super-block. Note Q6_K is asymmetric-free (scale only, no min), which is why it needs twice as many scales as Q4_K/Q5_K to hit the same width. Every K-quant shares the same super-block shape: QK_K = 256 values per block (ggml/src/ggml-common.h, `#define QK_K 256`), with K_SCALE_SIZE = 12 bytes of packed sub-block scales. block_q6_K = { uint8_t ql[QK_K/2];      // 128 bytes: LOWER 4 bits of each 6-bit quant uint8_t qh[QK_K/4];      // 64 bytes: UPPER 2 bits of each 6-bit quant, 4 quants per byte int8_t scales[QK_K/16]; // 16 scales, FULL 8-BIT (int8), one per 16 elements ggml_half d; }.  2+16+128+64 = 210 bytes / 256 values = 6.5625 bpw, matching the header comment. Verified task shorthand: q6_K IS pure 6-bit, and its sub-block scales are int8, NOT the 6-bit packed scales of q3_K/q4_K/q5_K. It has no per-block minimum (x = a*q) and, unlike q2_K/q4_K/q5_K, needs no second fp16 super-block scale. 16 blocks of 16. Q6_K IS NOT A MIXTURE: llama-quant.cpp's llama_tensor_get_quant_type maps LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_Q6_K straight to GGML_TYPE_Q6_K with no per-tensor promotion. It is however frequently used as the PROMOTION TARGET inside Q3_K_M/Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M mixtures (use_more_bits layers get Q6_K), so a Q4_K_M file contains real Q6_K tensors. The tool's own numbers on Llama-3-8B: Q6_K is +0.0217 ppl, versus Q5_K_M +0.0569 and Q8_0 +0.0026 (qlab2-quantize-options-table) - Q6_K is the last k-quant that is effectively lossless, and is the usual 'I want no quality risk and will pay the bytes' choice. Weight-only: activations stay FP16/BF16 at runtime. No accelerator has a k-quant path in silicon. Note block_q8_K is NOT a storage format: ggml-common.h comments it as 'only used for intermediate quantization and dot products' (a float32 scale, 256 int8 quants and 16 int16 block sums), so llama.cpp promotes activations to q8_K for the dot product rather than storing weights in it.
